title: Security Deposits Reinstatement Averaging Window by Length of Connection
content:
For a Security Deposits deposit reinstated on the waiver reinstatement basis, the averaging window over which the reinstated account's bills are averaged depends on how long the account has been connected: the whole months from the connect date on its Electric Service by Rate Schedule account to today.

## Schedule of windows

| Whole months connected before today | Window average |
|---|---|
| fewer than 24 (the short-history months) | the average bill of every billing period since the account's connection |
| 60 or more (the long-history months) | the average bill of the twenty-four billing periods immediately before today |
| at least 24 but fewer than 60 | no other window is set by this schedule |

An account connected fewer than **24** months before today is averaged over every billing period since its connection; an account connected **60** months or more is averaged over the twenty-four billing periods immediately before today.

## How a window average is read

The window average is the usage lines billed in the window added together, divided by the number of facility charge lines billed in the same window; each facility charge line marks one billing period.

## Edges of the bands

| Whole months connected | Window |
|---|---|
| 23 | every billing period since connection |
| 24 | not set by this schedule |
| 59 | not set by this schedule |
| 60 | the twenty-four billing periods immediately before today |

## Hypothetical illustration

An account connected 15 whole months ago has, since connection, usage lines totalling $2100.00 and 15 facility charge lines: its window average is $140.00. An account connected 72 whole months ago with $7200.00 of usage lines and 24 facility charge lines in the last twenty-four months has a window average of $300.00.
